title: A pilot study evaluating acceptability and feasibility of a group intervention for perfectionism
summary:
Perfectionism is increasingly understood as an underlying factor in the development and maintenance of various mental disorders. Accordingly, psychotherapeutic interventions have already been developed to specifically reduce perfectionistic experiences using classical cognitive-behavioural methods and to achieve improvements in the psychological distress of affected individuals. However, these previously developed interventions show high dropout rates, which limits the clinical utility of these treatments. Characteristics typical of perfectionism, such as rigidity and particularly critical self-evaluation, may require more specific treatment approaches, which are currently not available.

Our research project aims to develop a 4-week group psychotherapy intervention based on “third-wave” cognitive behavioural therapy methods (focusing on mindfulness, self-compassion, and acceptance). The aim is to design a more precise treatment option for affected individuals and perfectionism-specific problems and evaluate its feasibility. Furthermore, the intervention is intended to address a healthcare gap: The 4-week programme is designed as a basic group psychotherapy intervention, which has rarely been offered by clinical psychologists due to the lack of validated treatment manuals, but which could serve as a foundation for patients with perfectionism prior to potentially longer-term therapy.

The primary aim of this pilot study is to examine the acceptability and feasibility of a group psychotherapy intervention specifically designed for individuals with perfectionistic tendencies. The implementation of this pilot study serves as preparation for a subsequent clinical study that will evaluate the newly developed intervention on a larger scale. Changes in clinical measures and perfectionistic experiences resulting from treatment will be assessed but will not be the primary focus of analysis.
A total of 15–27 adults who meet the ICD-10 criteria for at least one mental disorder and show elevated levels of perfectionism will be recruited for this pilot study. During the initial screening, elevated perfectionism will first be assessed online, followed by a clinical screening interview to verify the presence of a clinically relevant mental disorder and diagnosis.

After inclusion, participants will be randomly allocated into three groups of 5–9 participants each, which will start the intervention at different time points (multiple-baseline design) to control for time effects. Participants will complete a structured 4-week group therapy intervention consisting of one session per week (100 minutes per session), conducted by licensed clinical psychologists. Participants will complete psychological assessments at different time points: 4–6 weekly assessments before the start of group therapy; 4 weekly assessments during group therapy, each immediately after the session; and one assessment 4 weeks after the end of treatment. Participation in this study is voluntary and can be terminated by participants at any time without disadvantages. All data will be treated confidentially and analysed in a way that prevents conclusions about individual participants.

interventions.name: Manualised transdiagnostic group therapy (4 sessions of 100 minutes each) with a focus on perfectionism and “third-wave” approaches (ACT; CFT)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients (≥18 years) will be included who have sufficient German language skills to actively participate in the group therapy. Eligible participants must demonstrate elevated levels of perfectionism (FMPS-CM score ≥29) and meet criteria for at least one mental disorder according to ICD-10, as validated by the Mini-DIPS.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria include the presence of a mental disorder requiring acute treatment due to risk of self-harm or harm to others, as well as substance dependence without established abstinence. Participants will also be excluded if they do not demonstrate general suitability for group therapy (assessed by licensed clinicians), are currently undergoing ongoing psychotherapy parallel to the study group therapy, and/or report a change in psychopharmacological medication within the previous 30 days prior to the beginning of screening.
